pr_title: Bluetooth: ISO: Add check for pending ISO connections
pr_body:
Per the HCI spec it is not possible to send the
HCI_LE_Create_CIS command while an outstanding request
is pending. To avoid failing the command we can
check and verify if any ISO connections are in the
pending state.
    
Since multiple ISO channels can be connected
in a single request, the solution implemented was
to iterate over all ISO connections and see if there was
any unicast ISO channels in the connecting state.
    
It also checks for the encryption pending state, as
we should not start the encryption procedure if we know
that the connect ISO command cannot be completed afterwards.

This adds a new return value to bt_iso_chan_connect,
and decided to properly document the return values the
function can return.

Signed-off-by: Emil Gydesen <emil.gydesen@nordicsemi.no>

fixes https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/issues/46829
pr_comments: I don't have the necessary understanding of ISO to review this PR in its current form. If you would like to me to, you will have to make the description more accessible.

> I don't have the necessary understanding of ISO to review this PR in its current form. If you would like to me to, you will have to make the description more accessible.

Fair. I had hoped that my commit message was explicit enough, but I guess not :)

Basically what this PR does is similar to the 
```c
	if (atomic_test_bit(bt_dev.flags, BT_DEV_INITIATING)) {
		return -EALREADY;
	}
```

check in `bt_conn_le_create`. 

It is slightly more elaborate with ISO as you can request connection for more than 1 ISO connection at a time (unlike ACL which is only one connection), and that there will be generated an event for each ISO connection in the request. 

So basically we have

```c
bt_iso_chan_connect(param, 4)
```
that will generate 4 events (since we are creating 4 connections). It is only once all 4 events have been received that we can call `bt_iso_chan_connect` again. 

This PR, instead of adding another flag, simply checks the state of all CIS (connected ISO), when calling `bt_iso_chan_connect`, and if anyone of them are in the connecting (or encrypting) state, then we reject the request.

Than you for the explanation. But I still don't understand what the purpose of this change is. AFAIU, without this change, the controller will just deny the HCI command. Isn't that ok? You are skirting around the "(or encrypting)"-bit like it's not important, but I suspect that this is the real reason behind this change. The commit message / PR description needs some love. Please rewrite it so it's obvious what motivates this change.

> Per the HCI spec it is not possible to send the HCI_LE_Create_CIS command while an outstanding request is pending.

I found this sentence in the spec: "If the Host issues this command before all the HCI_LE_CIS_Established events from the previous use of the command have been generated, the Controller shall return the error code Command Disallowed (0x0C)." Is that all you are referring to?

> Since multiple ISO channels can be connected in a single request, the solution implemented was to iterate over all ISO connections and see if there was any unicast ISO channels in the connecting state.

Non sequitur. What was the problem that needed a solution? The fact that 'multiple ISO channels can be connected in a single request' does not describe a problem, nor does it motivate the solution.

> It also checks for the encryption pending state, which is an additional check to make it simpler to handle in the ISO layer, as once security have changed we would not want to have to check for other pending ISO connections.

The construction of this sentence is really awkward. It should be split up and reworded. What is the ISO layer? The whole change is in `iso.c`, so I assume you have something more specific in mind. Please explain the problem carefully and why the solution works. What security change? (I actually don't know.) Why do we need to care if there are other "pending" ISO connections when security changes? How messy would it be if we did the check? Why do we not need the check with the change in PR?

> Than you for the explanation. But I still don't understand what the purpose of this change is. AFAIU, without this change, the controller will just deny the HCI command. Isn't that ok? 

Technically it is OK, but we would much rather avoid sending the HCI command if we know it will fail. We do that for almost all HCI commands in the host (and this is the primary issue that is being solved). 

> You are skirting around the "(or encrypting)"-bit like it's not important, but I suspect that this is the real reason behind this change. 

To some extend, it is true that this is one of the reasons behind this change, i.e. there's no reason to start encryption if we know the next procedure (i.e. actually sending the HCI command) will fail, but this is not the main reason. 

> The commit message / PR description needs some love. Please rewrite it so it's obvious what motivates this change.

The motivation of this change is that we don't want to send an HCI command that we know will fail. I think this is already covered by the commit message by

> Per the HCI spec it is not possible to send the HCI_LE_Create_CIS command while an outstanding request is pending. Since multiple ISO channels can be connected in a single request, the solution implemented was to iterate over all ISO connections and see if there was any unicast ISO channels in the connecting state.

 
> > Per the HCI spec it is not possible to send the HCI_LE_Create_CIS command while an outstanding request is pending.
> 
> I found this sentence in the spec: "If the Host issues this command before all the HCI_LE_CIS_Established events from the previous use of the command have been generated, the Controller shall return the error code Command Disallowed (0x0C)." Is that all you are referring to?

Yes

> > Since multiple ISO channels can be connected in a single request, the solution implemented was to iterate over all ISO connections and see if there was any unicast ISO channels in the connecting state.
> 
> Non sequitur. What was the problem that needed a solution? The fact that 'multiple ISO channels can be connected in a single request' does not describe a problem, nor does it motivate the solution.
 
That part describes the solution, and not the problem. The problem is stated earlier in the commit message. 

> > It also checks for the encryption pending state, which is an additional check to make it simpler to handle in the ISO layer, as once security have changed we would not want to have to check for other pending ISO connections.
> 
> The construction of this sentence is really awkward. It should be split up and reworded. What is the ISO layer? The whole change is in `iso.c`, so I assume you have something more specific in mind. Please explain the problem carefully and why the solution works. What security change? (I actually don't know.) Why do we need to care if there are other "pending" ISO connections when security changes? How messy would it be if we did the check? Why do we not need the check with the change in PR?

I can rewrite this paragraph, and add additional information - I do, however, not want to explain how the entire ISO architecture is designed and how it works as part of a commit that doesn't change any behavior except returning an error earlier by not sending a command that is known to fail to the controller. 

In this context `iso.c` is the ISO layer, and I used that term because ISO is implemented as a layer on top of `conn.c` (sort of as an extension of conn.c for a specific type of connection), but it may have been the wrong term to use :)
I also updated the commit message slightly

> @alwa-nordic Maybe it will be simpler to understand, and be a simpler implementation, if we just added a another `BT_DEV_` flag (e.g. `BT_DEV_ISO_INITIATING`).

No, the method of detecting if `HCI_LE_Create_CIS` is busy is fine. I was a bit confused about what `BT_ISO_STATE_ENCRYPT_PENDING` meant. I think I understand this PR now. I think it is as follows. I approve this PR now. If you want to use any of this text in the commit message or code comments, you are welcome to do so and I will re-approve.

If there are channels in `BT_ISO_STATE_ENCRYPT_PENDING` state, a `bt_iso_chan_connect` procedure is already ongoing, and the procedure detected that an ACL security upgrade was needed (and automatically requested it). The use of `HCI_LE_Create_CIS` has been deferred until the security is sufficiently upgraded. The `bt_iso_chan_connect` procedure holds an imaginary exclusive lock on `HCI_LE_Create_CIS` to ensure it's able use it immediately when the the security is sufficiently upgraded, instead of having to implement some form for waiting on this lock.

If there are channels in  `BT_ISO_STATE_CONNECTING` state, `bt_iso_chan_connect` procedure is already ongoing, and currently using `HCI_LE_Create_CIS`. That means the exclusive lock on `HCI_LE_Create_CIS` is not available. So if the security upgrade is needed, it does not have the lock it requires. And even if a security upgrade is not needed, attempting to use `HCI_LE_Create_CIS` will fail anyway.

issue_context.title: LE Audio: Avoid multiple calls to `bt_iso_chan_connect` in parallel
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
The HCI spec mandates that only 1 `BT_HCI_OP_LE_CREATE_CIS` command (triggered by `bt_iso_chan_connect`) can be outstanding at any time. 

**Describe the solution you'd like**
We should verify that no outstanding connection requests are pending before we call `bt_iso_chan_connect` in BAP (and possibly also a check in iso.c). 

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
N/A

**Additional context**
N/A

review_comments:
This could be simplied if we have an easy way of saying "or the return values from `bt_conn_set_security`. 

If anyone can suggest a wording where we can rely on the documentation from other (public) functions (such as `bt_conn_set_security`) that would be greatly appreciated (and would also make it easier to keep up to date if the return values of `bt_conn_set_security` changes).
